A central bank that views a 1 percent fall in output below yn as more costly than a 1 percent rise above yn will tend to err in the direction of an overly expansionary policy. As a result, an average inflation bias reemerges even though k 1⁄4 0. Ruge-Murcia (2003a), in contrast, considered the case of a central bank with an inflation target and asymmetric preferences over target misses. He showed that if the central bank prefers undershooting its target rather than overshooting it, average inflation will tend to be less than the target inflation rate.
